blindSummary:
The customary peace-pact system of a constituent jurisdiction in this state/province — bilateral inter-tribal pacts with their own holders, sanctions and dispute-resolution authority over “crimes and tribal-related offences” — was formally codified in February 2026 as a 137-page written pact. The country's national courts recognise the system; academic literature frames it as legal pluralism in which indigenous and formal criminal justice coexist, with national police handling customary-law cases. For a visitor whose dispute falls under a peace-pact jurisdiction, the applicable institution may not be a national court.

No trans-specific customary ruling, customary exclusion, or gender-expression punishment was documented in the dossier. Constitutional recognition of indigenous justice also appears in the basic law of the country's autonomous territory, reinforcing the framework.
